design.contrast: interruption versus equal-count, position- and folio-matched ordinary gap; include section and line-position nuisance controls
design.falsifier: No held-folio interaction after controls, or an effect explained by page position/line length alone, falsifies the reset-state mechanism; do not rescue it by changing boundary thresholds.
design.mechanism: A drawing interruption clears the active owner/item state and begins a new process segment; ordinary transcription spaces do not.
design.prediction: After interruptions, first fields have higher rates of explicit owner/item introduction and lower anaphoric continuation than after matched ordinary gaps, replicating across held folios and alternate readings.
design.related: DIC001_drawing_interruption_target; drawing_reset_segment_atlas; DIC001 limitations explicitly prohibit picture-ownership or translation claims
design.scope: cached admitted transcription and DIC001/segment-atlas boundary inventory only; feasibility unknown for a clean owner/item coding panel
design.unit: eligible interruption and matched ordinary gap on the same folio/page, with adjacent cached fields

summary: Test whether the 440 unanimous drawing interruptions define a semantic state reset: the first complete field after an interruption should reintroduce an owner or item cue, while an ordinary same-page gap should usually continue the prior state. This retains DIC001's distributed-reset result and the drawing-reset segment atlas, but does not infer picture ownership, words, or translation.
title: Drawing interruptions reset inherited process state

design.contrast: ordinary line break without interruption versus matched within-line continuation and interruption-adjacent line break
design.falsifier: A line-break penalty equal to or larger than the interruption penalty, replicated in held folios, falsifies nonreset continuity; do not reinterpret line ends as clauses after the fact.
design.mechanism: Physical line layout is not a semantic closure boundary; state continuity is broken by drawing interruption, not by line ending.
design.prediction: Owner/item recurrence and compatible argument slots remain continuous across ordinary line breaks at rates comparable to within-line continuations, but drop after interruptions; section-specific classes remain separate.
design.related: DIC001_drawing_interruption_target; drawing_reset_segment_atlas; SIDEQUEST_scribe_memory (historical proposal only); GDT791 line-boundary correction
design.scope: cached 30-page owner-spine and admitted prose selectors; feasibility unknown for complete state labels outside the released owner panel
design.unit: adjacent line pairs within cached running prose, stratified by interruption status and folio

summary: Test the rival to a line-as-clause reading: when no DIC001 drawing interruption occurs, a line break should preserve the active owner/item state into the next line, while an interruption should reset it. The proposal uses the same admitted segment and visual-owner scope but asks a different state-transition question from DIC001.
title: Ordinary line breaks preserve local owner and item state

design.contrast: edge occurrence versus matched non-edge occurrence, crossed with ordered register pair and section; leave-one-register-pair-out validation
design.falsifier: No held edge interaction, or improvement disappears when whole identity and host class are controlled, falsifies the handoff mechanism; a global class lead is not sufficient.
design.mechanism: A whole at a register boundary signals transfer of the active record or target between adjacent presentation modes; its role depends on the ordered source/target register pair.
design.prediction: A small set of whole forms shows reproducible edge-specific continuation/owner-slot changes for one or more ordered register pairs, beyond whole identity, position, section, and host-class baselines.
design.related: post_IL023_system_class_heterogeneity_correction; GDT790_panel_owner_image_grammar_overlay; GDT792_host_transfer; these predecessors do not test ordered register-edge interaction
design.scope: admitted visual-owner spine and cached text/register tags; feasibility unknown for enough held transition edges, and no new page access is assumed
design.unit: complete-whole occurrence within one field of a cached register transition, with non-edge occurrences of the same whole as controls

summary: Test whether complete whole forms at immediate transitions between running prose, local labels, and radial units act as handoff markers, rather than having one global meaning or merely reflecting section frequency. The design follows the post-IL023 correction by fitting register-specific classes and evaluates only an edge interaction.
title: Register-transition edges carry handoff roles

design.contrast: role association on all-reading intersection versus each reading-specific surface; hold out physical folios
design.falsifier: A role survives only in one reading, or vanishes when uncertain spaces are preserved, falsifies the semantic claim; do not promote a reading-specific form meaning.
design.mechanism: A genuine whole-level role is attached to the underlying inscription locus and is stable across admitted alternate readings.
design.prediction: A candidate role retains direction and material effect on the all-reading intersection and in at least two independent reading projections after section, position, and folio controls.
design.related: GDT859 alternate-reader alignment; GDT764 bounded fields; current route's explicit prohibition on treating EVA labels as phonetic units
design.scope: cached source-group atlas and admitted semantic occurrence panels; feasibility unknown for candidate roles lacking complete three-reading joins
design.unit: complete-whole occurrence with a raw-group identity and three available reading projections

summary: Treat ZL3b, IT2a, and RF1b as alternate readings of one manuscript and test a necessary condition for any proposed complete-whole role: the role contrast must remain when forms are joined at raw-group identity and evaluated under each reading. A role lead that exists only after one reading's spacing or glyph choice is not semantic evidence.
title: Semantic role must survive alternate raw readings

design.contrast: candidate whole's incompatible-slot rate versus matched control wholes with the same frequency, section, and position profile
design.falsifier: Repeated held-folio counterexamples in the preregistered incompatible slot, or no separation from frequency/position controls, rejects the role claim and leaves the whole opaque.
design.mechanism: A concrete role imposes a semantic incompatibility boundary, so an item-like whole cannot freely occupy a process-only slot (and conversely).
design.prediction: At least one independently held candidate role shows a low incompatible-slot rate with a fixed upper bound, while matched opaque controls do not; a positive association without exclusion is insufficient.
design.related: GDT770 target-masked valency tournament; GDT805 context-role discriminator; GDT762 role candidates; this proposal adds a negative necessary-condition gate rather than another role fit
design.scope: cached exact-whole occurrence panels and existing structural tags; feasibility unknown until compatible/incompatible slots are frozen without using the target outcomes
design.unit: complete-whole occurrence paired with a predeclared compatible/incompatible structural slot

summary: For any candidate role that claims a concrete function such as quantity carrier, nominal item, or process operator, test its required negative context: the same complete whole should be rare or absent in a preregistered incompatible slot after matching section, position, and neighboring frame. This is a counterexample screen, not a positive classifier.
title: A proposed role requires exclusion from incompatible slots

design.contrast: A-to-B frame transfer and B-to-A frame transfer versus matched non-synonym pairs with equal frequency and edit distance
design.falsifier: A directional transfer fails on held folios or is no better than matched non-synonym pairs, falsifying shared-role interchangeability; do not rescue with component decomposition.
design.mechanism: Shared semantic role licenses the same neighboring argument and closure frames in both directions, subject to register-specific controls.
design.prediction: A genuine same-role pair passes both directional held-folio transfers with stable slot polarity; one-direction-only pairs are classified as analogies or distinct roles.
design.related: GDT807 target-masked paragraph exchange; GDT746 whole analogy distribution; GDT770 valency masking; this freezes reciprocal direction as the necessary condition
design.scope: cached complete-field and whole-neighbor panels; feasibility unknown for pairs with fewer than two independent physical folios per direction
design.unit: ordered complete-whole frame: immediate left/right whole and structural tags around one target

summary: When two complete wholes are proposed as the same role or interchangeable variants, require reciprocal frame compatibility: each must occur in the other's independently observed left/right structural frames, with held examples in both directions. One-way analogical similarity cannot establish a shared meaning.
title: Candidate same-role wholes require reciprocal frame compatibility
